finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar passes a client-supplied avatarUrl straight to axios.get. The only check is that the value is a string starting with 'https://', which does not restrict the destination host, address range, or redirect targets. An attacker can make the server issue GET requests to internal hosts, loopback, link-local/cloud metadata addresses, or any other reachable service, including via an https:// URL that redirects to http://. The response body is not returned; the client only gets its byte length (and a 2xx vs. non-2xx difference, since errors are unhandled), so this is primarily blind SSRF with a size/status oracle.
finding.source: server.js:10 — req.body.avatarUrl (POST /profile/avatar, no authentication, JSON body parsed by express.json() at server.js:5)

trace.note: express.json() parses the attacker-controlled request body
url = req.body.avatarUrl taken directly from the request body, no normalization
axios.get(url) issues the outbound request; no host allowlist, no IP/private-range block, no redirect restriction, no response size cap
Only img.data.length is returned to the caller, so the response content is not directly reflected

finding.guards_checked: (1) Type check: url must be a string. Does not limit destination. (2) Scheme check: startsWith('https://'). Does not limit host: https://169.254.169.254/, https://localhost:<port>/, https://10.x.x.x/, https://users.internal:8080/ all pass. Also bypassed by an https:// URL that 30x-redirects to http:// or to a private IP, because axios follows redirects by default and no maxRedirects or re-validation is set. (3) No hostname allowlist, DNS resolution check, or private/loopback/link-local IP block anywhere in server.js. (4) No response size limit. (5) No timeout. Not a finding: USER_SVC at server.js:7 is a hardcoded host, and the id at server.js:19 is encodeURIComponent'd so '/', '?', and '#' cannot change the host or escape the path (only bare '.'/'..' segments remain, which resolve within the same fixed host and are not SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: Only a type check and scheme prefix check at server.js:11 (typeof url === "string" && url.startsWith("https://")), which does not restrict host, IP range, or redirects. No auth middleware on the route (server.js:9, app.use at server.js:5 is only express.json), no hostname allowlist, and no response size or redirect limit anywhere in server.js.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) reaches axios.get at server.js:14 on an unauthenticated route, and the only guard at server.js:11 is a scheme-prefix check that does not limit the destination host, so the SSRF is real; the trace lines all match the file.
